packSplit.rule: The public fact source contains only the core packs registered in system.json: coc-skills (60 documents) and coc-professions (9 entries). Extension-only facts and build inputs are maintained outside this repository; no extension pack is declared or emitted here.
packSplit.customTemplate: custom-investigator is a product-defined core template (evidence: product). It is not a printed occupation and no sourceRefs claim that any source prints it; its eight skills, 0-99 Keeper-reviewed credit rating and five whitelisted point formulas are a product decision.

scope: M1 core skills, derived attributes, success bands, growth and starter isolation; M2 first-batch occupations, occupation point formulas, credit-rating ranges and creation/allocation rules; M3 native combat (bonus/penalty d100, weapon profiles, opposed/fight-back/cover, extreme damage, situational modifiers) and wounds (major wound, dying, death, First Aid, Medicine, weekly and natural healing); M4 native sanity/insanity, Luck spend and recovery, skill growth and the persisted CoC world clock; M5 core specialisms and the Doctor of Medicine / Police Detective records retained in the core set; M6 Science (Astronomy) retained as a core skill; M7 Science (Zoology) and Science (Forensics) retained as core skills plus the core Antiquarian occupation. M4 rule facts and evidence grades live in content/coc/sanity-provenance.json. Extension-only occupations were moved out of the public repository.

licenseBoundary.facts: Only numeric values, formulas, field semantics, skill names and URLs from official public Chaosium sources or the user's coc-cardwright repository are recorded. Prose in this repository is written for this project.
excluded: No Call of Cthulhu 7e Foundry VTT system source, template, YAML or implementation was read or referenced.
No other GPL system implementation was used.
No coc-cardwright visual template, HTML/CSS, Python implementation or repository code is copied; only numeric occupation facts, formulas, credit ranges and skill names are mapped.
No official PDF, text block, image, font, logo or trade dress is committed.
No claim is made that VTT use is covered by Chaosium's fan material policy; VTT use is a maintainer decision and third-party rights remain with their owners.

No occupation description, skill-list prose or page layout from Roll20, Chaosium or coc-cardwright is reproduced; only the point formula, credit-rating range and skill names needed for data mapping are recorded.
No GPL Call of Cthulhu system implementation, template or source file was read or referenced for this batch.

sources.title: Official wiki: Combat
usedFor: Initiative is DEX order; a readied firearm acts at DEX +50
Dodge tie goes to the defender; fight back needs a strictly higher success band
A winning fight back deals regular damage only
Extreme damage: blunt maximum weapon damage + maximum damage bonus; impaling adds the damage bonus and another weapon die
Only the initiating attacker can deal extreme damage
Firearms cannot be fought back; a target may dive for cover with Dodge (attacker penalty die, diver forfeits next attack)
Firing 2-3 shots in a round gives one penalty die per shot; point blank (one-fifth DEX in feet) gives one bonus die
Fighting maneuver: each point of Build deficit gives one penalty die, capped at two; a deficit of three or more is ineffective
Outnumbered: after the defender has fought back or dodged this round, further melee attacks get one bonus die; firearms ignore it

sources.title: Official wiki: Hit Points, Wounds, and Healing
usedFor: Damage in one blow at or above half full HP is a major wound; the character rolls CON or falls unconscious
A major wound at zero HP is dying: CON at the end of each round or die; First Aid stabilizes
Damage at or above maximum HP in one blow is instant death
Zero HP without a major wound is unconsciousness only
No major wound: +1 HP per day; major wound: weekly CON, +1D3 (extreme +2D3), cleared by an extreme success or HP back to half
First Aid: +1 HP, rouses an unconscious character, extends a dying character's life
Medicine: +1D3 with at least an hour and equipment; a dying patient becomes eligible for weekly healing

combat.evidence: primary (official wiki pages) for the rules; no official weapon table is bundled

implemented.dice: bonus/penalty tens dice as one real Nd10 pool (1 units + 1+net tens), 00+0=100, 00+n=n, one bonus cancels one penalty
implemented.difficulty: required success band (regular/hard/extreme); the target is never multiplied
implemented.characteristicTest: rolled against the characteristic value itself
implemented.weaponSkill: weapon.system.skill1/skill2 brpid (+ CoC specialism key), live skill total; never the display name
implemented.unarmed: 1D3 + full DB, explicit flags.brp.coc.weapon marker; the BRP special:'crush' field is ignored
implemented.damageBonus: melee full, thrown/bow half (halved die), firearms none
implemented.extremeDamage: blunt max weapon + max DB; impaling max weapon + DB + another weapon die; computed in pure code because the compat Roll ignores maximize
implemented.opposed: band, then skill, then a fresh pair of rolls on an exact tie (lower d100 wins)
implemented.closeCombat: dodge tie -> defender; fight back needs a strictly higher band and deals regular damage only
implemented.firearms: no fight back; dive for cover on a successful Dodge -> attacker re-rolls with one penalty die, diver forfeits next attack
implemented.modifiers: 2-3 shots -> penalty die; point blank (DEX/5 ft) -> bonus die; maneuver Build deficit 1-2 -> penalty dice, >=3 ineffective; outnumbered melee -> bonus die (firearms exempt)
implemented.wounds: current HP written straight to system.health.value; state under flags.brp.coc.wounds; major wound CON, dying per-round CON, instant death, unconscious at zero without a major wound
implemented.healing: First Aid +1/stabilise, Medicine +1D3, weekly CON (1D3 / extreme 2D3, clears major wound), natural +1/day without a major wound
implemented.exclusions: no BRP wound items, no health.daily accumulation, no hit locations; useHPL is ignored and recorded as hplIgnored
implemented.unopposed: a target that declares no defence is a legal state: the attack resolves on its own band and the damage lands on the declared target (choice 'none')
implemented.cardIsolation: a second attacker never joins another actor's open attack card; reuse is gated on the same initiator with a single attacker entry
implemented.hitLocations: CoC actors never enter the BRP hit-location, armour-HPL or hit-location item creation branches (nor the sheet HPL mode), even when the world still has useHPL on; rerolled vitals also reset flags.brp.coc.wounds
implemented.xp: CoC difficulty never skips a development tick (the target is never multiplied); Cthulhu Mythos (noXP) never ticks; octopus keeps its own skip rule

unimplemented: Weapon catalogue: only the native unarmed weapon and user-created weapon items are supported
Critical (01) extra damage beyond the extreme tier
Burst/full auto, dual wield, aiming, cover values, range-difficulty modifiers
Monster armour/damage reduction and multi-attack action economy
Per-combatant initiative override for readied firearms
Automated weekly calendar healing (the weekly check is an explicit API call)
Frontend/studio combat tab and browser E2E (compat repository)

occupations.evidenceNote: Every profession in the public core set is secondary evidence only. No record claims an official first-party Chaosium source. The first batch rests on the Roll20 compendium (itself a transcription of the Free Basic Rules). Doctor of Medicine and Police Detective additionally cite the public Chaosium wiki. Antiquarian is sourced from the user coc-cardwright repository, which states that its occupation and skill data came from trpg-saikou and its rule calculations reference cochar; that statement is recorded as the repository chain, not as independent first-party confirmation.

coc7.occupation.private-investigator.formulaNote: Published as EDU*2 + (STR*2 or DEX*2): the player picks one characteristic. Replaces the earlier MAX(DEX,STR) reading.

coc7.occupation.doctor-of-medicine.skillShape: First Aid, Other Language (Latin), Medicine, Psychology, Science (Biology), Science (Pharmacy) + any two

coc7.occupation.police-detective.formulaNote: Published as EDU*2 + (DEX*2 or STR*2): the player picks one characteristic. Not modelled as MAX(DEX,STR), which would hand out a strictly larger pool. Kept as an ordered either/or list so the builder can present the choice.
coc7.occupation.police-detective.skillShape: Art/Craft (Acting) or Disguise, Firearms, Law, Listen, one interpersonal skill (Charm/Fast Talk/Intimidate/Persuade), Psychology, Spot Hidden + any one

coc7.occupation.antiquarian.skillShape: Accounting, Appraise, Drive Auto, History, Library Use, Navigate, two interpersonal picks (Charm/Fast Talk/Intimidate/Persuade)
coc7.occupation.antiquarian.claimBoundary: Mapped one-to-one from coc-cardwright's jobs.py; no public occupation page was consulted for this record. The repository is secondary evidence and is not an official Chaosium publication.

notes: The Dilettante page body is empty in the compendium; only its attributes block (credit 50-99, EDU*2+APP*2, Firearms, Ride, and four choice groups) is available, so the record relies on the attributes block alone.
No occupation outside these four batches is claimed. Occupations lacking a verified formula or credit range must not become a character-creation default.

Explorer, Private Investigator and Soldier publish a characteristic choice (Explorer APP/DEX/STR; Private Investigator and Soldier STR/DEX). All three were previously modelled as MAX(...) and are now ordered either/or formula lists; the player picks one and the engine refuses to allocate until a choice is pinned. No MAX formula is used by any shipped occupation.
Police Detective is an either/or occupation that must not be collapsed: the source says DEX*2 OR STR*2, so it stays an explicit two-formula choice (EDU*2+DEX*2 / EDU*2+STR*2) and never a MAX.

Police Detective is a separate occupation from Private Investigator: different credit band (20-50 vs 9-30), different formula wording, Law/Listen/Spot Hidden fixed with no Library Use, and an Art/Craft (Acting)-or-Disguise slot. Neither record aliases the other.

The M7 batch (the four M6 records re-sourced plus 19 new occupations) cites coc-cardwright only. Its jobs.py prints the formula, credit range and complete skill list for each entry; no public occupation page was read or spliced for these records. Skill names were mapped to the project's existing stable keys; the eight-slot shape is the jobs.py list, except where a productNote records an earlier product decision.

coc-cardwright's README states that its occupation/skill data come from trpg-saikou and its rule calculations reference cochar. That chain is recorded as the repository's own statement. Only facts were mapped; no visual template, HTML/CSS or Python implementation was copied.
UGE minWealth/maxWealth are not credit rating and are never read or written as one.

No record here is a first-party Chaosium source. The licensed-compendium records are still transcriptions, the community-page records are secondary cross-checks, and the coc-cardwright records are a secondary transcription as well. Treat the whole file as secondary evidence and record any later official confirmation separately.
Science and Art/Craft specialisms take the family base (Science 1, Art/Craft 5) rather than an individually printed value; the family base is the verified fact and the specialism inherits it.
The specialism names are confirmed by the occupation skill lists that require them; the printed base chance is the family base on the 1920s sheet.
No name here is a first-party Chaosium statement about the specialism table; the occupation pages are the evidence that these specialisms exist under those parents.
Science (Astronomy) inherits the Science family base of 1 from the 1920s sheet; no individual printed value is claimed.
Its existence under the Science parent is confirmed by the Pilot occupation list, which fixes Science (Astronomy) alongside Pilot (Aircraft).
No name here is a first-party Chaosium statement about the specialism table.
Both specialisms take the Science family base of 1; coc-cardwright's skills.py gives 科学(动物学) and 科学(鉴证) an initial value of 1.

coc-cardwright's README records trpg-saikou as the upstream data source and cochar as the rule-calculation reference; that chain is recorded as the repository's statement, not as first-party confirmation.
